title: Regional route convergence surgeon notes
content:
Executive summary:
This is a working incident review + runbook draft for handling slow route convergence after partial regional edge degradation. The doc captures a recent on-call execution where weighted DNS shifts plus progressive egress rehoming produced extended tail latencies and inconsistent KV cache warmup across regions. The purpose is to standardize the 'convergence surgeon' role (operator responsible for coordinating traffic-smoothing, DNS TTL, and KV cache preseed) and produce a minimal repeatable checklist.

Incident snapshot:
- Date/time window: 2025-02-11 18:32 UTC -> 2025-02-11 22:10 UTC
- Affected region: eu-west-2 primarily, with spillover to us-west-2 as routing rehomed
- Symptoms: elevated token-latency 95/99 percentile for generation endpoints, increased DROPPED=true responses originating from edge nodes, significant cache-miss ratio on model KV cache warmup (kvcache_miss_rate spiked from 4% -> 42%) during weight shifts
- Customer visible impact: longer response times for hosted-api customers pinned to eu-west-2; some short-lived 5xx spikes during route convergence windows
- Root cause (hypothesis at time of writing): simultaneous weighted DNS rebalancing and edge BGP flaps led to uneven traffic redistribution while KV caches were cold in target region; automatic burst scaling kicked in but initial cold-start latency cascaded due to client retries and small per-request timeouts.

What went well:
- Canary routing rules prevented total outage: canary percentage held at 5% for first 10m as intended
- Observability surfaced kvcache miss rate and region-level capacity metrics quickly (dashboards & alerts)
- Operator coordination channel established (sre-oncall + net + runtime) and was used continuously

Failures / gaps:
- No explicit orchestration step to preseed KV cache before increasing weight beyond 30%
- DNS TTL change was applied without accounting for intermediate CDN egress caches leading to stale client-side resolution patterns
- Lack of a single 'surge decision document' — multiple ad-hoc operator actions created inconsistent rollback thresholds

Convergence surgeon runbook (draft):
Purpose: coordinate a safe, observable, reversible regional traffic shift with explicit KV cache prewarm and DNS/edge TTL handling.
Roles:
- Surgeon (on-call SRE): executes weight changes, tracks metrics, calls canary gates
- Net lead: applies DNS/edge config changes and verifies propagation
- Runtime lead: pre-seeds KV cache, ensures model processes ramp correctly
- Incident comms: external/internal messaging

Pre-shift checklist (surgeon):
1) Telemetry sanity checks (baseline):
   - Ensure kvcache_miss_rate < 6% in target region before any weight above 5%
   - CPU/GPU headroom >= 20% on target autoscaling groups
   - Control plane latency (controlplane_req_p99) < 80ms
2) Prepare warmup pods: request runtime lead to run kvcache preseed job:
   - Command (runtime): ./tools/preseed_kvcache --model X --region eu-west-2 --token-prefixes seeds/charge-sets --parallel 8 --timeout 15m
   - Validate: kvcache_miss_rate trending down to <8% after preseed
3) DNS/edge preparation (net):
   - Verify edge caches TTLs (CDN) for our apex and subdomain: curl -I https://edge-host/eval
   - Coordinate TTL change: do not reduce global TTL below 30s unless emergency; prefer using weighted DNS with current TTL
4) Communication: announce start time + rollback plan on incident channel and post an update to status page if customer visible

Shifting traffic (surgeon step-by-step):
- Start: set weight to canary 5% for 10 minutes. Observe: p95 latency, kvcache_miss_rate, error rate.
- Gate: if p95 increases >20% relative baseline OR kvcache_miss_rate > 15% OR error_rate increase >0.5%, abort and rollback to previous weights.
- If stable, step weights up in increments: 5% -> 15% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%. Wait between steps: 10m, 12m, 15m, 20m.
- After passing 30% and 60% gates, ask runtime to ensure kvcache saturation: target kvcache_miss_rate < 5% and sustained request token latency drop.
- If any gate fails, execute weighted rollback (reverse increments) and request emergency preseed + hold at 0-5% until manual review.

Operational command snippets (examples):
- Check DNS weights: gcloud dns policies describe-weighted --name=myservice-routing --region eu-west-2
- Apply weight (cli shim): infra-tools route-weight set --service hosted-api --region eu-west-2 --weight 15
- Query kvcache metrics: prometheus_query 'sum(rate(kvcache_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kvcache_lookup_total[5m]))'
- Check edge cache headers: curl -I -H 'Host: hosted-api.redwood.ai' https://edge.example | egrep 'Cache|Age|Via'
- Force preseed job (kubernetes): kubectl apply -f jobs/preseed-euw2.yaml && kubectl logs -f job/preseed-euw2

Rollback criteria (quick reference):
- p95 latency > 1.5x baseline for 10m consecutive AND error_rate increase > 0.3% -> immediate rollback by halving weight
- kvcache_miss_rate > 20% for 5m -> immediate pause and request full preseed run
- Control plane API error spikes (5xxs) -> divert to fallback region and open incident bridge

DNS-specific notes:
- Avoid TTL flips during mid-shift unless unavoidable; lowering TTL can increase DNS PRs and amplify resolver churn. Prefer weighted DNS changes with existing TTL.
- For emergency fast-evacuations, coordinate with CDN provider to purge or reduce edge TTLs on impacted prefixes (note: purges cause downstream re-resolves).
- Keep a list of conservative resolver prefixes (corporate vs global) — some resolvers ignore low TTLs and will hold old answers longer; include this in decision-making

KV cache warmup guidance:
- Preseed with representative prefixes reflecting top 100 user prompt shapes. Random prefixes will not converge as efficiently.
- Use parallelism tuning: default 8 workers for medium models, 16 for large models, but watch GPU memory pressure.
- Keep a moving-window kvcache hit target of >95% after full ramp for production flows.

Post-incident telemetry to capture (for retrospective):
- Weighted DNS change timestamps + TTLs seen by major public resolvers (Google/Cloudflare/OpenDNS)
- Per-region kvcache_miss_rate 1h before -> 2h after
- Client-side retry patterns (idempotent vs non-idempotent)
- Autoscaling events (scale up/down) during shift
- BGP flap logs / edge peering state changes if present

On-call notes from the run (raw):
- 18:40: Marco noticed kvcache_miss_rate jumping; asked runtime to kick off preseed.
- 18:47: Initial 5% canary looked OK but p95 increased 18% baseline -> held at 5% to observe.
- 19:10: Edge reported transient 502s from origin due to connection churn from new edge nodes; rolled back to 3% for 8m.
- 19:25: After preseed completed, miss rate fell from 42% to 9% over 12m.
- 19:40: Progressed to 30% weight. Within 7m p95 was stable, but we saw higher 99th until kvcache hit threshold.
- 20:12: Final ramp to 100% completed with close monitoring; small customer impact noted but resolved within 30m window after final preseed pass.

Action items / follow-ups:
- (runtime) Build an automated preseed job that can be kicked by route-weight controller, tracked by a new preseed_job_status metric (JIRA-SRE-4521). Due: 2025-03-14, owner: Benji Solano.
- (net) Add edge-cache-propagation tests to canary pipeline to estimate effective TTL across major CDNs (CONFLUENCE-7894). Due: 2025-03-21, owner: Elena Park.
- (sre) Add a new Alert: kvcache_miss_rate > 10% sustained for 10m during any weight change window; link to runbook. Due: 2025-03-01, owner: Aisha Kumar.
- (product) Update customer-facing runbook templating for pinned-region SLAs to include prewarm expectation language. Due: 2025-03-07.

Open questions / notes for discussion:
- Should route-weight controller automatically trigger preseed when weight > 30%? Failure modes if preseed takes too long?
- How aggressive can we be with TTL changes without causing resolver churn in common enterprise resolvers? Run lab tests.
- Can we provide a per-customer fallback policy that pins requests to last-known-good region for N minutes?

Appendix: quick commands cheatsheet for surgeons (copyable)
- route-weight set: infra-tools route-weight set --service hosted-api --region eu-west-2 --weight 30 --author "oncall"
- preseed kick: kubectl create job --from=cronjob/preseed-euw2 preseed-manual-$(date +%s)
- observe metrics: curl -s "https://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(kvcache_miss_total[5m]))/sum(rate(kvcache_lookup_total[5m]))" | jq .

Notes on document status:
This is intentionally a collaborative, living runbook. Feedback welcome on the gating thresholds, wait times, and command implementations. Once we've validated the automated preseed controller (JIRA-SRE-4521) we'll move this to the final runbook set and add a short training playbook for on-call drills.
